findings.evidence: Never `git add -A` or `git add .`: they sweep in untracked artifacts. Never `git commit -a` or `-am` either: they stage every modified tracked file
findings.fix: Keep the never-list (it blocks a real agent shortcut). Move the flag explanations, which current models already know from git help, into one clause, and record the shortened wording in docs/audit/recovery/commit-work/record.md.

findings.evidence: Never propose `--no-verify`, not even as an option; use it only when the user asks for it by name, because it skips the checks the repository relies on.
findings.fix: Add the non-obvious consequence: a passing retry after `--no-verify` reports a commit the repository's own hook rejected, so the report must say the hook was skipped.

findings.evidence: Read `references/commit-message-template.md` only when the repository sets its own message rules (commitlint config, commit template, CONTRIBUTING, PR template), you need footers beyond `BREAKING CHANGE`, or you want worked messages.
findings.fix: Split the trigger: load it for repository rules, extra footers, or the commitlint defaults; add Do NOT Load it when writing one default Conventional Commits message for an empty repository.

findings.evidence: Which index? Commit request and the user has staged content that must stay out: a temporary index
findings.fix: Name the case where approved paths and the user's staged paths are disjoint: `git commit -- <approved paths>` commits those paths and leaves the user's index entries untouched. Keep the temporary index for mixed hunks, approved staged blobs, and any path that also has unstaged edits.

findings.evidence: Verify the staged version with the fastest relevant check: tests for the touched paths, else lint, else build.
findings.fix: Add the default when several checks exist: run the repository's test command scoped to the touched paths; fall back to lint, then build, only when no test command exists.

findings.evidence: "id": "review-and-commit" ... "Shows ordered `git status`, `git diff`, `git add -- src/auth.ts`, `git diff --cached`, and `git commit` commands."
findings.fix: Add one eval whose prompt has an approved path with both an approved staged diff and extra unstaged edits, asserting the staged blob is committed with `git diff --cached --binary` and `git apply --cached` and the unstaged edits stay out. Soften the review-and-commit assertion so it checks the ordered review and a path-scoped stage, not one exact command sequence.

findings.evidence: If `git diff --quiet` succeeds and no untracked file feeds the check, run it in place. Otherwise the tree is not the commit: export the index
findings.fix: Before the in-place branch, require `git diff --quiet` and an empty `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard`. An untracked source file that is part of the approved commit makes the in-place run test a tree the commit does not contain.

findings.evidence: When the user approved a path's staged diff, commit that exact staged version and never restage the whole working-tree file over it
findings.fix: State the overlapping case: an approved staged blob plus unstaged hunks in the same path is captured with `git diff --cached --binary` and applied to the temporary index; `git add -- <path>` is forbidden for that path.

findings.evidence: The routing table has a 'review what is staged | steps 1 and 4, report findings | change the index or the tree' route. trigger-queries.json covers it ('before i push, look over what i've got staged'), but none of the 18 output evals exercises it.

findings.evidence: 'export the index with git checkout-index -a --prefix=<run>/verify/'. <run> is created inside the git dir, so the export path contains '/.git/'. Some runners, such as Jest's haste map, ignore files under VCS directories, so the check finds no tests and exits non-zero. The agent then reports a test failure that is not real.
findings.fix: Add a sentence after the export command: 'If the runner reports no tests found or no files matched in <run>/verify/, it is ignoring paths under .git: export to mktemp -d outside the repository instead (same link and cleanup rules), or report "staged version not verified"; never treat it as a test failure.'

findings.evidence: Step 3: 'Search the whole repository ... for the legacy APIs ...: `components=`, ... `<Grid item`, ...'. A literal search for '<Grid item' misses multi-line JSX where 'item' sits on the next line after '<Grid', and those legacy props are 'silently ignored' (Gotchas). The migration can therefore miss hits and still pass the typecheck.
findings.fix: Say to search for each prop name on its own (for example a multiline search for '<Grid[^>]*\bitem\b', or the bare 'item' prop inside Grid elements), then confirm with the typecheck. Note that 'components=' also matches non-MUI props, so check each hit's import before migrating it.
